$comment: DRAFT SKETCH — rough JSON, format NOT final (format v0 is ticket #10). This is the MVP acceptance workflow: the pipeline the engine must run end-to-end. Vocabulary follows CONTEXT.md.
name: release-notes
$comment_worker: Workflow-level default worker: prompt steps below carry no worker field and inherit this. Binary steps override to the local engine.
$comment_config: Config flows in from outside (author/operator), inherited downward. No step ever writes it.

input.$comment: Top-level input object is empty; everything arrives via config.

output.$comment: Output object: { file: <path of written release notes> }.

body.$comment: Mechanical assertion: fail fast if the range produced nothing.

payload.prompt: From the raw git history in your input, summarize the user-facing FEATURES as a markdown bullet list. Ignore fixes and chores.
From the raw git history in your input, summarize BUG FIXES and internal improvements as a markdown bullet list. Ignore new features.
Write release notes in markdown from the feature and fix summaries in your input (the collected outputs of the parallel block). Audience: users of the project.

body.$comment: Judge-step pattern: judgment happens in a normal LLM step that outputs a verdict; the checkpoint after it only mechanically tests that verdict.

payload.prompt: Judge the release-notes draft in your input. Output STRICT JSON only: { "pass": boolean, "feedback": string, "suggested_format": "short" | "long" }. pass=true only if accurate, complete, and readable.

body.$comment: Bounded loop per the MVP logicer decision: exceeding max_iterations fails the run, so anything after this loop can assume the draft passed.
Nested workflow by relative path (workflow-as-step). Fresh, isolated context inside; data crosses only via input/output objects.
Branch-arm matching semantics are still open in ticket #11; sketch assumes first-matching-arm-wins.

payload.prompt: Condense the release notes in your input to at most 10 bullets under a single heading.
Expand the release notes in your input into sections (Features / Fixes / Details) with a short intro paragraph.
